Rashi on Shabbat 110a:1:1.hebrew: בר קשא - ממונה למלך, וישראל היה:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:1:1.english: Bar kasha - [He was] an official of the king, and he was a Jew.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:1:2.hebrew: דילמא חיויא דרבנן - שעבר על נידוי חכמים, ונחש הנושכו על כך אין לו רפואה. לפיכך, לא נמצא לו רפואה:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:1:2.english: Perhaps a snake of the Rabbis [bit him] - [It means] that he transgressed a ban of the Sages, and a snake that bites him on account of this has no cure; therefore, no cure was found for him.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:1:3.hebrew: אין רבי - אין רבינו, כך היה:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:1:3.english: Yes, my teacher - Yes, our teacher, so it was.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:1:4.hebrew: דכי נח נפשיה דרב גזר רב יצחק - שיהיו ממעטים משמחה אותה שנה, ולא יהא אדם מביא אסא וגידמי להילולא בטבלא, שהיו רגילים להביא הדס וענפי דקלים לשמוח לפני החתן והכלה, וכשמביאים אותן לפניהם, מקשקשים לפניהם בשוק בבואם בתופים וזוגין. טבלא — אשקליט"א. וגזר שלא יקשקשו לפניהם עוד:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:1:4.english: When Rav passed away, Rav Yitzḥak decreed - That they should diminish rejoicing that year, and that no person should bring myrtle and [palm] branches to a wedding with a tavla [bell]; for they were accustomed to bring myrtle and palm branches to rejoice before the bride and groom, and when they would bring them before them, they would ring [bells] before them in the street as they came with drums and bells. Tavla — eschelete [Old French: a small bell]. And he decreed that they should no longer ring [them] before them.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:1.english: Whom [a snake] encircled - [It] coiled around him.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:10.hebrew: בי כוכבי - במקום גלוי, שלא יעלה דרך הגג ויפיל עצמו עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:10.english: Under the stars - In an open place, so that [the snake] will not climb up via the roof and drop itself upon him.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:11.hebrew: שחפי - ענפים וקסמים, וכל דבר המקשקש זה בזה ומשמיע קול כשיעבור הנחש עליהן, וירגישו החתולים ויאכלוהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:11.english: Shachafei - Branches and wood chips, and anything that rattles together and makes a sound when [the snake] passes over them, so that the cats will notice [it] and eat it.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:12.hebrew: בי חלתא - בין החולות, שאין נחש יכול לרוץ שם, ויחזור לאחוריו:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:12.english: In sand - Among the sands, for a snake cannot run there, and it will turn back.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:2.english: And let him invert a dikula - A basket.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:3.english: On its head - Of the snake, above his [own] head.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:4.hebrew: וליהדקיה מיניה - יוריד הסל מעט מעט לצד הנחש, ויבדיל בו הנחש מבשרו שיעלה על הסל, שאם אוחזו בידו או מנתקו בחזקה, יכעוס וישכנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:4.english: And push it away from him - He should lower the basket little by little toward the snake, and separate the snake from his flesh with it so that it climbs onto the basket; for if he grabs it with his hand or tears it away forcefully, it will become angry and bite him.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:5.hebrew: וכי סליק - הנחש על הסל, ימהר וישליכנו במים ויברח לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:5.english: And when it climbs - [i.e.,] the snake onto the basket, he should hurry and throw it into the water and flee.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:6.hebrew: דמיקני ביה חיויא - כועס ורודף אחריו, ומריח ריח פעמיו ורודפו:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:6.english: At whom a snake is angry - [The snake] is angry and pursues him, and smells the scent of his footsteps and pursues him.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:7.english: Let him ride him four cubits - So that the tracks of his footsteps will be interrupted, and [the snake] will not be able to smell them.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:8.english: Let him jump [over] a ditch - Let him leap [over] a trench of water.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:2:9.english: Four barrels - So that [the snake] will not climb up to him quickly and will not smell his scent.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:3:1.english: Whether he has set his mind upon her - For the desire of sexual intercourse.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:3:2.english: She should remove her garments - She should strip off her clothes and throw them in front of her.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:1.english: What is the remedy - if [the snake] sets its mind upon her.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:10.english: Fragrant - That has a good aroma.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:11.english: And let them place [them] there - On the ground beneath her seat.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:12.hebrew: וליטרוקינהו בהדדי - היין והשחליים, כדי שיעלה הריח:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:12.english: And let them mix them together - [That is,] the wine and the cress, so that the fragrance will rise.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:14.hebrew: דאי לא - קלי ליה, הדר עילוה:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:14.english: For if [he does] not - burn it, it will return upon her.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:2.english: She should have relations before it - With her husband, and [thereby] become repulsive before it.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:3.english: And throw [them] at it - And she should throw [them] at it.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:4.hebrew: דשתנא אנא - דרך נשים לי, ולחש בעלמא הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:4.english: Dishtana ana - "The way of women is upon me," and it is merely an incantation.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:5.hebrew: דעייל בה חיויא - כשהוא תאב לה, נכנס כולו באותו מקום:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:5.english: Whom a snake has entered - When it desires her, it enters completely into that place.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:6.english: Let them spread her [legs] - They should spread her legs apart from one another.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:7.hebrew: אתרתי חביתי - מקצתה על זו ומקצתה על זו, כדי שיפתח רחמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:7.english: On two barrels - Part of her on this [one] and part of her on that [one], so that her womb will open.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:8.english: And throw [it] onto coals - So that the scent will rise.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:4:9.english: A bowl of cress - A basket full of garden cress.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:5:1.hebrew: לאיתויי טחול לשינים - ואע"פ שקשה לבני מעיים:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:5:1.english: To include spleen for the teeth - Even though it is harmful to the intestines.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:5:2.hebrew: כרשינין לבני מעיים - ואע"פ שקשה לשינים, כדאמרינן בברכות (דף מד:), סד"א כיון שקשים לאדם, לאו אורחיה למיכלינהו אי לאו לרפואה שיש בהם, ומוכחא מילתא וניתסר — קמ"ל:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:5:2.english: Vetch for the intestines - And even though it is harmful to the teeth, as we say in Berakhot (44b), you might have thought to say [that] since they are harmful to a person, it is not his way to eat them unless for the healing [property] that is in them, and [thus] the matter is evident and it should be prohibited; [therefore, the Gemara] teaches us [that it is permitted].

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:5:3.english: Capers - The fruit of the caper bush, [in Old French:] caprier.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:6:1.hebrew: תלאי - דקלים, נטיעות מין תמרים שנקרא בלשון ארמי תאל"י:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:6:1.english: Talai - Palm trees, saplings [of] a species of dates that is called in the Aramaic language ta'alei.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:6:2.english: The first cup - that they drink from that water.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:6:3.english: Loosens - [the] waste in the intestines slightly.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:6:7.english: So too they emerge - For they cleanse the intestines of the excrement from the first [cups].

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:6:8.hebrew: והוא דלא רגיל - למשתי שיכרא, כבר עברו מ' יום:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:6:8.english: And provided that he is not accustomed - to drinking beer, [i.e.,] forty days have already passed [since he last drank it].

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:7:1.hebrew: רב יוסף אמר זיתום המצרי - הוא מי דקרים, ועל שם שדוקרים את החולי:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:7:1.english: Rav Yosef said: Egyptian zitom - It is mei dekarim [piercing water], and [it is so called] because it pierces the illness.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:7:3.hebrew: סיסני - כלי שנותנין בו תמרים, כדאמרינן בעלמא (ב"מ דף סז:): ואי אגבהינהו בסיסני קננהו. וסימניך דלא תחליף שמעתתא: שם כלי זה יהא לך סימן, שיש בו שני סמכין — רב יוסף אמר שערי:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:7:3.english: Sisanei - A vessel in which dates are placed, as we say elsewhere (Bava Metzia 67b): "And if he lifted them in sisanei, he acquired them." And [regarding] "your mnemonic," so that you do not confuse the teachings: the name of this vessel shall be a mnemonic for you, for it has two samekhs — Rav Yosef said barley [se'arei].

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:7:4.english: Between the slaughter [of the Paschal offering] and Atzeret - Between Passover and Atzeret [Shavuot].

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:8:1.english: Alexandrian gum - Resin of trees from Alexandria.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:8:2.hebrew: גביא גילא - אלו"ם בלע"ז:

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:8:3.hebrew: כורכמא רישקא - כרכום של גן, קרו"ג אוריינטל, הגדל בגנים:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:8:3.english: Garden saffron [kurkema rishka] - Saffron of the garden, [in Old French:] croc oriental, which grows in gardens.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:8:4.english: For a zava - Let one give her those three kinds [of ingredients] to drink in wine.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:8:5.hebrew: ולא מיעקרא - אינה נעקרת מלילד, לפי שהיין מפיג חוזקן של סמנים ומתרפאה מן החולי:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:8:5.english: And she does not become barren - She is not rendered barren from bearing children, because the wine weakens the potency of the herbs, and she is healed from the illness.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:8:6.hebrew: לירקונא תרי - מינייהו לישתי בשיכרא, וזהו רפואתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 110a:8:6.english: For jaundice, two - of them he should drink in beer, and this is his cure.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:8:8.english: For a zava, three with wine - [The Gemara] mentions it again because of those [other] remedies that it proceeds to list.

Rashi on Shabbat 110a:8:9.english: And if not, etc. - All of them are beneficial only for a zava.

Tosafot on Shabbat 110a:1:1.hebrew: חיויא דרבנן טרקיה דלית ליה אסותא - אע"ג דגבי בן דמא, בן אחותו של ר' ישמעאל, בפרק ב' דמס' ע"ז (דף כז:), קאמר שלא עבר על דברי חבירים, שנאמר: "ופורץ גדר ישכנו נחש", אע"ג דלא הוה ליה אסותא, שהרי מת — התם לא היה לו רפואה מזומנת; אבל הכא, שהרפואה היתה מזומנת ונאבדה ממנו במזל רע, קאמר דלית ליה אסותא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 110a:1:1.english: "A snake of the Rabbis bit him, for which there is no cure" - Even though regarding Ben Dama, the nephew of R' Yishmael, in the second chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (27b), it says that he did not transgress the words of [his] colleagues, as it is stated: "and one who breaches a fence will be bitten by a snake," even though he had no cure, for indeed he died — there, he did not have a cure readily available; but here, where the cure was readily available and was lost from him through bad fortune, [the Gemara] says that "there is no cure for it."

Tosafot on Shabbat 110a:4:1.hebrew: וליתי אגנא דתחלי - משמע הכא דהנחש אוהב שחליים, וכן בשלהי דנדרים (דף צא:) דקאמר ליה נואף לבעל: "לא תיכול מהני תחלי דטעמינהו חיויא", וא"כ יש בהן משום גילוי. ובפרק ב' דמס' ע"ז (ל: ושם) אמר דשחליים אין בהם משום גילוי! וי"ל דהתם לא ממש שחליים קאמר, אלא בהנך דאמר התם (מס' ע"ז דף סז.): "וכן היו עושין בערבי שבתות בצפורי [נותנין חומץ לתוך גריסין] והיו קורין אותו שחליים". אי נמי בשילהי נדרים (דף צא:) מיירי דהוה ביה חלא, כדמסקינן התם במס' ע"ז (דף ל:): "אבל אית בהו חלא — מיגרי בהו". והכא נמי, חמרא מיגרי בהו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 110a:4:1.english: And let them bring a bowl of cress - It is implied here that the snake loves cress, and similarly at the end of Nedarim (91b), where the adulterer says to the husband: "Do not eat of this cress, for a snake has tasted it" — and if so, it is subject to [the prohibition of] uncovered [food]. Yet in the second chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (30b, and there), it says that cress is not subject to [the prohibition of] uncovered [food]! And one can answer that there it does not literally mean cress, rather [it refers] to that which it says there (Tractate Avodah Zarah 67a): "And so they used to do on Shabbat eves in Tzippori [they would put vinegar into pounded beans], and they would call it cress." Alternatively, at the end of Nedarim (91b) it is referring to [a case] where there was vinegar in it, as we conclude there in Tractate Avodah Zarah (30b): "However, if there is vinegar in it, [the snake] is attracted to it." And here as well, the wine attracts [the snake] to it.

Tosafot on Shabbat 110a:7:1.hebrew: רב יוסף אמר זיתום המצרי - ר"ת כל הך מילתא מחק מספרו, ואומר דל"ג אלא בריש אלו עוברין (פסחים מב:). ונראה לר"י שמחקה משום דזיתום המצרי מותר לשתות, כדתניא בפרק בתרא (דף קנו.): "ושוין שבוחשין את השתית ושותין זיתום המצרי". ואומר ריב"א דאין צריך למחוק, דרב יוסף לא קאי לפרש מי דקרים דמתני', אלא אמילתיה דעולא קאי, דאמר: שיכרא בבלאי מעלי מינייהו, ואומר רב יוסף דזיתום המצרי מעלי מינייהו. מיהו משמע כפירוש הקונט' דאמתני' קאי, מדלא קאמר בהדיא "זיתום המצרי מעלי מינייהו":
Tosafot on Shabbat 110a:7:1.english: Rav Yosef said: Egyptian zitom - Rabbeinu Tam erased this entire statement from his book, and he says that we do not recite it [here], but rather at the beginning of [the chapter] Eilu Ovrin (Pesachim 42b). And it appears to Rabbi Yitzchak that he erased it because Egyptian zitom is permitted to drink [on Shabbat], as it is taught in the last chapter [of this tractate] (156a): "And they agree that one may stir shetit and drink Egyptian zitom." And Riva says that there is no need to erase [it], for Rav Yosef is not referring to explain "water that stabs" [mei dekarim] of the Mishnah; rather, he is referring to Ulla's statement, who said, "Babylonian beer is more effective than them," and Rav Yosef says that Egyptian zitom is more effective than them. However, it seems [to be] like Rashi's explanation that he is referring to the Mishnah, since he does not state explicitly, "Egyptian zitom is more effective than them."

Tosafot on Shabbat 110a:7:2.hebrew: סיסאני - ולא קאמר "וסימניך סמך סמך", כדאמר בשילהי במה אשה (לעיל שבת סו.), משום דשערי לא כתיב בסמך:
Tosafot on Shabbat 110a:7:2.english: Sisanei - And [the Gemara] does not say "and your mnemonic is samekh samekh," as it says at the end of [the chapter] Bameh Ishah (above, Shabbat 66a), because se'arei [barley] is not written with a samekh.
